clue.text: Slip by government calculator

parts.note: to slip is to slide
rule is government, as in direct rule

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks past an official using a pocket calculator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Before electronic devices, engineers did multiplication on this sliding logarithmic scale, a mechanical calculator.

clue.text: Tract of grassland left uncultivated

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for meadow or grassland

indicators.note: uncultivated land is left wild and disordered, so the letters of 'left' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stretch of meadow has been allowed to run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like a stretch of land, matching the grassland in the surface, but it means a pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet pushing a cause, which is a small printed handout.

clue.text: Urge along to fashionable type of American cinema

parts.note: to drive cattle is to urge them along
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Someone is pushed towards a trendy American picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans watched films from parked cars at an open-air screening venue.

clue.text: Put at ease now that someone else has taken over

definitions.text: now that someone else has taken over

explanation.surface: A worker feels calmer once a colleague takes the next shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved means comforted, and also describes a sentry or worker whose shift has passed to a replacement.

clue.text: Frenchman who couldn't adapt to new regime?

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters of 'regime' are reformed

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat could not cope after the Revolution brought a fresh government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges REGIME; 'to' is a link word. The surface fits the definition: émigrés were aristocrats who fled revolutionary France.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was first used for royalists who left France after 1789, unable to live under the revolutionary state.

clue.text: Mostly at home with the officer

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: Usually the officer is to be found at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or as a rule, the same as mostly.

clue.text: Towed home

parts.note: a dwelling pulled behind a car: a mobile house on wheels

explanation.definitionFit: This trailer is a living space that holidaymakers hitch to a car and pull along.

clue.text: Respect for the Queen in the Ministry

indicators.note: in places the Queen's letters within the ministry's name

parts.note: the Ministry of Defence, shortened to Defence
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Civil servants show reverence for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'the' are link words; the Ministry of Defence is the British government department for the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is humble regard or courteous submission, which is respect.

clue.text: Charge the chap given time

parts.note: a chap is a man
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A man is given a set time to answer an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests an accusation but means an instruction or commission; 'the' and 'given' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official commission or order, a charge given to someone.

clue.text: Minute causes of ill-feeling

parts.note: read 'minute' as tiny and 'ill-feeling' as sickness: microscopic germs, not small grudges

explanation.definitionFit: These rod-shaped bacteria are tiny organisms that cause disease.

clue.text: Handy missile?

parts.note: a weapon thrown by hand, as the phrase 'hand' plus the bomb's name suggests

explanation.definitionFit: This small bomb, often called a hand bomb, is lobbed by a soldier's arm.

clue.text: Sad boy flagged?

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective hinting at a flag; the answer is the flag itself

parts.note: blue means sad
Peter is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A gloomy lad is singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a blue signal flag with a white square, flown when a ship is about to sail; '?' marks the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval signal for imminent departure is a pennant, so the name is literally a flag.

clue.text: Property that produces results

explanation.surface: A piece of land turns out to be productive.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal effects are belongings; effects are also outcomes or consequences that work produces.

clue.text: Join in league on free date arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of 'free date' are reordered

explanation.surface: Teams agree to join a league on a date with no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to unite states or clubs into an alliance or federation.

clue.text: One's standing in golf

parts.note: not a ranking on the tour but how a player physically places their feet when addressing the ball

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's posture and foot position over the ball is called their address position.

clue.text: Request to smile while being shot

definitions.text: Request to smile while being shot

parts.words: Request to smile while being shot
parts.note: 'shot' means photographed: what a photographer says before taking the picture

explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask subjects to utter this phrase because it forms a grin.

clue.text: Is able to include a river boat

indicators.note: the first piece wraps around the others, so it is opened to hold them

parts.note: can means is able
the Tamar is a river between Devon and Cornwall in England

explanation.surface: Someone manages to fit a river vessel in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing vessel.

clue.text: Supplements needed for a theologian to finish article

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
to end is to finish
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Extra material is required so a divinity scholar can complete an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed for' and 'to' are link words; 'article' is a grammatical article, not an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the end of a book, extra sections to complete it.

clue.text: Is able to discourage holding the bottle

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
can means is able

explanation.surface: Someone manages to put a drinker off the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bottle' looks like slang for courage, but it is the glass vessel; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a stoppered glass vessel for serving wine or spirits.

clue.text: Bankers' bloomers

explanation.surface: City financiers make embarrassing mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bankers' suggests financiers and 'bloomers' blunders or underwear; a flow-er has banks, a flower blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers have banks, so a 'flower' is something that flows; bloomers are blossoms in a garden.

clue.text: Pass time, the French returning, splitting peas

indicators.note: returning means the French article is read backwards

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

indicators.note: splitting breaks the word peas apart so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone passes the hours shelling peas, French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' looks like it wants something inserted into the peas, but it signals the anagram that follows the turned French article.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or goes by.

clue.text: Made an assortment on Sunday of wreaths

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixture, so the letters of 'made an' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A florist made a variety of garlands on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment' rearranges MADEAN as ANADEM; 'on' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is an old poetic word for a garland or chaplet for the head.

clue.text: Sink a coal-carrying vessel

explanation.surface: A coal barge goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately; a coal scuttle is a bucket for fuel by the fire.

clue.text: A case for holding bottles of wine, one sort of wine including the Spanish

definitions.text: A case for holding bottles of wine

indicators.note: including means the wine's name holds the Spanish word

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A wine case holds bottles, including some Bordeaux and a Spanish one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or sideboard for storing wine bottles.

clue.text: Oriental flower festival

parts.note: E is short for east or ...
an aster is a daisy-like garden plant

explanation.surface: A celebration of eastern blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' tempts a river, but here it is a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Christian spring feast of the Resurrection.

clue.text: As of equal value to silver American vegetable

parts.note: at par means of equal value
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A US vegetable is as precious as silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green spear-shaped shoot eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Covers up wrong answer quietly inside

indicators.note: inside places the quiet letter within the jumbled letters
wrong means the word answer is set out incorrectly, in a jumbled order

parts.note: p (piano) means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone hides an incorrect reply under their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ANSWER as ENWRAS, and 'inside' puts P within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwrap is to wrap something round, enclosing and covering it.

clue.text: Witnesses at the games

parts.note: tests are Test matches, international cricket games

explanation.surface: Spectators turn up at the sporting matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witnesses' is a verb here, and 'the' is a link word; Test matches are international cricket games.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true.

clue.text: Water Board expert on top!

parts.note: surf is breaking waves on the shore
an ace is an expert, here one on the board

explanation.surface: A specialist at the regional water utility is the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water Board' reads as a utility company, but it is surf and a surfboard; a surf ace rides on top of the water. 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface of something is its uppermost face or outer layer.

clue.text: Remedied with fresh bandages on?

explanation.surface: A nurse puts it right by applying new bandages.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to put it right; a wound re-dressed has new dressings applied.
